I'd pick these three, based on the most recent awards and guides I could find:

1. **La Gran Tasca (Chamberí).** It won "Best Cocido Madrileño 2025" in the 15th Ruta del Cocido Madrileño, a public-vote award announced in February 2026. It has been open since 1942 and serves cocido every day. The stew takes 48 hours to make and has 15 ingredients, and Time Out says the restaurant served about 19,600 cocidos in a year. One search result placed it near Teatro Real instead, so check the address before you go.
   Source: [Time Out Madrid – "el nuevo rey del cocido en Madrid"](https://www.timeout.es/madrid/es/noticias/este-restaurante-familiar-abierto-en-1942-es-el-nuevo-rey-del-cocido-en-madrid-48-horas-de-elaboracion-y-15-ingredientes-distintos-021326)

2. **La Bola (near Ópera).** This is the classic choice. The same family has run it for four generations since 1870, and it still cooks cocido in individual clay pots over embers for about four hours. It appears in the 2026 cocido guides.
   Source: [Guía del Ocio – "En estos restaurantes se toma el mejor cocido madrileño"](https://guiadelocio.es/madrid/en-estos-restaurantes-se-toma-el-mejor-cocido-madrileno/)

3. **Pancipelao.** The Club de Amigos del Cocido, a group of enthusiasts, gave its cocido the highest average score for 2026. That is a fan-club rating, not the official Ruta award.
   Source: [esdiario – "¿Dónde tomar todavía un buen cocidito madrileño a cuatro vuelcos?"](https://www.esdiario.com/chismografo/tendencias/260313/182310/todavia-tomar-buen-cocidito-madrileno-cuatro-vuelcos.html)
